children.name: 1.2 Education

children.name: 1.3 Health care

children.name: 1.4 Shock responsive systems for effective disaster and pandemic preparedness and response

children.name: 1.5 Inclusive Community engagement

framework.name: Sustainable, resilient and green economic growth and resource management

children.name: Outcome 2 - Economic Growth, Innovation and Climate Change

children.name: 2.5 DRR

children.name: 2.6 Sustainable cities

children.name: 2.1 Employment and skills development

children.name: 2.2 Sustainable and resilient economic growth and green and blue economy transition

children.name: 2.4 Climate and ecosystem resources

framework.name: Effective, people-centred governance, rule of law, human rights and gender equality
framework.description: Transparent and accountable institutions, delivering quality, inclusive services, enabling rule of law and increased access to justice, and implementing human rights commitments.

children.name: Outcome 3 - Governance, Rule of Law, and Human Rights
children.description: By 2026, governance is more transparent and accountable, enabling people (women and girls, men and boys, and persons at risk of exclusion), to enjoy quality, inclusive services, enhanced rule of law and access to justice in line with Albania’s human rights commitments

children.name: 3.1 Access to justice

projects.name: 2025 2.2.11 The capacity for quality and standards compliance is strengthened to facilitate market access for SMEs in the medicinal and aromatic plants (MAP) value chain and to support targeted products in the fruit and vegetable (F&V) value chain.
projects.description:
Albania’s economy is steadily growing, with strong export potential in selected sectors. Within the framework of the Global Quality and Standards Programme, the project aims to strengthen quality and standards compliance capacities in order to facilitate market access, with a primary focus on the medicinal and aromatic plants sector, while also generating spillover benefits for the food and vegetable sector.

In recent years, Albania has become one of Europe’s leading producers of medicinal and aromatic plants. Production has traditionally focused on wild-harvested plants such as sage, lavender and cornflowers collected in foothill areas; however, cultivation is increasingly shifting towards more commercial production models. The food and vegetable sector is more fragmented, although greenhouse producers in central Albania have demonstrated growing interest in improving product quality through the application of standards and accredited conformity assessment services.

As a secondary focus, the project targets fresh fruit and vegetable production in greenhouses located in the geographical triangle of Lushnja, Fier and Berat. Both the medicinal and aromatic plants sector and the food and vegetable sector face quality infrastructure-related challenges in demonstrating compliance with international market requirements, which constrain export opportunities.
